stories.head: Only 24% of companies have a company-wide AI policy as agent adoption races ahead, Liferay study finds
stories.plain: A Liferay survey of enterprises finds 54% are already running AI agents but only 24% have a company-wide usage policy and just 25% measure AI impact with clear KPIs. That gap between deployment speed and strategic oversight is exactly the risk that gets marketing AI projects defunded or regulated — making this a must-read for anyone buying or approving AI tools.

stories.head: Programmatic video AI decisions lack transparency, putting pressure on platforms to explain outcomes
stories.plain: AI is quietly making bid, placement, and targeting calls inside programmatic video that buyers can't easily audit. The piece argues platforms must explain AI-driven outcomes or risk losing marketer trust and budget. This directly affects how adtech is evaluated and governed, shifting the buying conversation from performance claims to explainability.

stories.head: Ahrefs launches Letaido, an agent-powered marketing workspace for multi-step autonomous workflows
stories.plain: Ahrefs has shipped Letaido, a workspace where marketing teams can plan and run multi-step agentic tasks — automating recurring workflows, building dashboards, and monitoring competitors — all natively connected to Ahrefs search data. It moves the category beyond AI chat assistants toward systems that actually act, which changes what teams expect from MarTech tools.

stories.head: directree launches GEO Monitor to track brand visibility inside AI engine answers weekly
stories.plain: GEO Monitor submits buyer-intent questions to five AI engines every week and reports which brands and sources appear in the answers — with no brand prompting. This is one of the first commercial tools for tracking generative engine visibility, making GEO measurable for software vendors and shifting SEO budgets toward AI-answer optimization.

stories.head: Deloitte becomes first global system integrator to deliver a Salesforce Forward Deployed Engineering engagement for AI-driven lead automation
stories.plain: Deloitte has staffed and completed the first GSI-led Salesforce Forward Deployed Engineering engagement, embedding engineers directly with a client to build AI-driven lead automation. This signals a new delivery model where big integrators co-build agentic CRM features on-site — changing how enterprises buy and implement marketing AI at scale.

stories.head: OpenAI adds product carousels and AppsFlyer attribution to compete for ad dollars
stories.plain: ChatGPT is adding product carousels and performance attribution via AppsFlyer, giving performance marketers the measurement hooks they need to shift real budgets into the platform. This moves OpenAI from an experimental ad channel to a measurable one — directly challenging Google and Meta for search-intent ad spend.

stories.head: Time magazine serves ads directly to AI crawlers in a novel GEO strategy
stories.plain: Time is placing ads inside pages targeted specifically at AI crawlers rather than human readers, aiming to embed brand messages into AI-generated answers. This is the first documented editorial brand using crawler-targeted advertising as a GEO tactic — a potential template for any publisher or brand wanting visibility inside AI responses.

stories.head: Liferay study: 54% of companies run AI agents but only 25% measure their impact
stories.plain: A large enterprise survey finds that adoption of AI agents is racing ahead of governance and measurement: most companies have no company-wide AI policy and no clear KPIs for agents. For anyone buying or approving agentic marketing tools, this data makes the governance gap concrete and hard to ignore.

stories.head: directree launches GEO Monitor for weekly AI visibility tracking across five AI engines
stories.plain: GEO Monitor submits buyer-intent questions to ChatGPT, Perplexity and three other AI engines weekly, then reports which brands and sources appear. It gives software vendors the first recurring, automated audit of their generative engine presence — making GEO measurable rather than anecdotal.

stories.head: Programmatic video AI decisions lack transparency, putting pressure on platforms to explain outcomes
stories.plain: As AI automates more bidding and placement decisions in programmatic video, buyers increasingly cannot see why their ads ran where they did. The piece argues platforms must build explainability into their systems — a governance issue that affects every marketer relying on automated ad buying.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Everywhere, Accountability Nowhere
body: A Liferay study found that 54% of companies are already running AI agents, yet fewer than one in four measure what those agents actually produce. Platforms like Brightspot, Suralink, and Ahrefs all shipped agentic workflow features this month, accelerating adoption further without pausing for measurement frameworks.

The governance gap is now the defining risk: businesses are committing budget & operational trust to autonomous systems before they have baselines for success. Leaders who establish measurable outcomes first will be able to justify — and safely scale — agent investments; everyone else is running experiments they cannot audit.
ev: Liferay Study · agent adoption vs. measurement gap

themes.head: AI Rewrites the Advertising Marketplace
body: OpenAI moved to capture ad revenue this month, while Time magazine debuted AI-only ad placements and a step-by-step guide appeared for running campaigns directly inside ChatGPT. These are not experiments — they signal a structural shift in where media budgets will flow as AI interfaces become primary discovery surfaces.

Programmatic buyers are simultaneously demanding more visibility into AI-driven bidding decisions, exposing tension between automation speed & advertiser control. Brands that learn to optimise for AI-curated environments now will hold an early-mover advantage as traditional search and social ad inventory loses share to conversational AI surfaces.

themes.head: Product Discovery Is Being Rewired by AI
body: AI assistants, publisher recommendation engines, & social media algorithms are converging into a single new discovery layer that sits above traditional search. This month's analysis shows consumers increasingly finding & evaluating products through AI-curated feeds rather than keyword queries, compressing the funnel in ways Google-era SEO cannot address.

Tools like directree's GEO Monitor — which tracks brand visibility inside AI answers weekly — show that marketers are scrambling to measure presence in this new layer. The strategic implication is clear: share of AI answer is becoming as important a metric as share of search, and the playbook for earning it is still being written.
ev: Agile Brand · directree GEO Monitor launch

themes.head: Governance & Privacy as Competitive Infrastructure
body: IAB Tech Lab released new privacy standards this month at the same moment AI prompt governance emerged as a cost & compliance issue for marketing teams. Separately, TransFi launched an AI compliance platform for cross-border payments, signalling that regulatory infrastructure is now a product category — not just a legal obligation.

For marketing decision-makers, the practical shift is that governance is moving from legal department to tech stack. Teams that embed privacy & prompt controls into their workflows early will avoid costly retrofits as regulation tightens; those who treat it as overhead will face both liability & operational drag.
ev: MarTech · IAB Tech Lab privacy standards
Agile Brand · TransFi JARVIS compliance platform

themes.head: Agencies & Teams Face an AI Skills Reckoning
body: Two complementary pieces this month — one on which marketing skills AI amplifies, another on how agencies are restructuring to survive AI — point to the same truth: AI is not eliminating roles so much as ruthlessly sorting talent. Strategy, creative judgment, & cross-functional coordination are rising in value; execution tasks are collapsing in price.

The organisational dimension shows up in Front's Kevin Yang arguing for speed without sacrificing coordination, and in research showing that budget conflicts over creative still kill campaigns before they launch. Teams that combine AI fluency with sharp human judgment on priorities & stakeholder alignment will outrun those that automate execution alone.
ev: MarTech · skills AI makes more valuable

month.takeaway: Across every corner of the feed this month, the central tension is the same: AI capability is outrunning the measurement, governance, and human-coordination systems needed to turn it into durable competitive advantage.
